summary: A clean restack of two measured gains on disjoint shapes: block-m two-smaller touches only bs>=128, the landed Triton post-norm only bs<32, and the code is the same one-line pick that already passed all 5 tests including bs=257. One run can be read. The only open item is the bs=256 pick (32 here, 16 in marlin-block-m-cap-16-port, which is still running), and that run's harvest answers it, not a companion.
justification: The mechanism is measured on this exact problem. Per-m-block Marlin cost grows with thread_m_blocks. next-larger lost 18-28%, next-smaller gained (bs=128 1.194, bs=256 1.151), and verify-two-smaller gained more (bs=128 468.8->343.7 us, 1.364; bs=256 618.6->468.7 us, 1.32). All of these ran on base fc28840b9d, whose bs>=128 path is byte-identical to master's: the post-norm patch only adds a num_tokens < 32 branch, and bs=128/256 still call SGLang's fused_post_expert_norm_weighted_sum. Master's bs=128/256 rows (475.9/622.2 us, Marlin 95-96%, 4.7x/5.7x SoL of 101/109 us) match the old base's 468.8/618.6 within drift, so the expected ~345/~470 us are well grounded. Headline check: each load is one shape and the score is a geomean over 6 loads, so swapping master's bs=128/256 per-shape speedups (1.001/1.000) for 1.364/1.32 multiplies the headline by (1.364*1.32)^(1/6) ~= 1.10, which predicts about 1.24x. The proposer's ~1.23x is consistent. The controls are right: bs=1/8/16 keep pick 8 plus the Triton post-norm, and bs=32 keeps 16 plus SGLang's combine, so they should reproduce master's 55/121/156/207 us. Weakest link: the bs=256 choice of 32 is not known to be the best point. Decode_layer's cap-16 gained at T=256, and cap-16-port (64->16 at bs=256) is in the judge right now. If 16 beats 32 at bs=256, this run lands a result that is already sub-optimal at one of six loads. Minor: the old-base profile shows bs=256 Marlin at 490.8 us against a 468.7 us shape median (profile and timed passes disagree), so judge this run by the timed median and the paired SGLang ratio, not the kernel sum.
confounders: post-expert-norm-triton-small-m (192f225d8f): not a confounder for the target shapes, since its branch is num_tokens < 32 only and bs>=128 keeps SGLang's combine unchanged. Its rows (bs=1/8/16) are the in-run control and should reproduce master. A drift of more than ~2.5% there means run noise, not interaction. If it were reverted, bs>=128 would be unaffected.

sglang-marlin-path-parity (a646cb4151): the foundation. block_size_m feeds moe_align_block_size over the 32-expert bank, so padding is 32*(bm-1) rather than 256*(bm-1), plus both Marlin calls. Smaller bm also cuts padded rows, but the old-base measurement had the same local-count align, so the measured gain already includes this interaction and carries over unchanged.
interference: No companion is needed. A gain at bs=128/256 can only come from the block-m pick, because nothing else in the timed path changes for those shapes, and the bs<128 rows are a built-in control on the same base. A loss would also be unambiguous: it would mean a bad restack or drift, and the controls would show which. The one real question is bs=256 at 32 versus 16. An ab-tune companion (this branch with the bs>=128 pick replaced by min(pick, 16)) would be the same code as cap-16-port restacked onto post-norm. That is a tuning choice settled by cap-16-port's harvest, which is already in flight. It is not needed to read this run. Recommended sequencing: hold dispatch until cap-16-port (base 150297e862) harvests. If its bs=256 row beats verify-two-smaller's 1.32 by clearly more than drift (more than ~3%), retune this spec's bs=256 pick to 16 before claiming, so that only one restack is spent. Otherwise dispatch as written. bs=128 is 16 in both, so nothing there depends on it.
open_questions: Does cap-16-port's bs=256 row (64->16) beat verify-two-smaller's 1.32 (64->32) by more than drift? If yes, change the bs=256 pick to 16 before dispatch, and do not run both restacks.

The bs=257 test now picks 32 on master's lineage (it passed on the old base). Its post-norm path is SGLang's at bs>=32, which is unchanged, so correctness risk is minimal, but confirm the 5/5 tests pass.

For the implementer: use BLOCK_SIZE_M_CANDIDATES.index(block_size_m) after the loop, as in the landed patch, so the loop-exhausted case (64) maps to index 4. Do not track idx inside the loop in a way that misses the exhaust case.
